findings.message: RUN001 FINDING, NOW RESOLVED at a7200d2 and verified this run: the four substantive accounts (OS types, file management, I/O chain, kernel layers) had no bound-excerpt support while the sources file claimed the excerpts carried them. The repair extended the ostep excerpt with chapters 39 and 36 (fetched from the book's site; this reviewer independently fetched the same three chapter PDFs and verified 20 of the 21 quoted passages verbatim), remapped the coverage matrix (U3-02 norton, U3-03/U3-05 ostep, U3-06 shellyVermaat), and rewrote the norton/shellyVermaat declarations to disclose title-level-only support for the OS-types and kernel-layers accounts - the honest D-2026-0001 option-(c) posture. Two smaller defects the repair introduced or left are recorded as new findings F5 and F6 below.

RUN001 FINDING, NOW RESOLVED: rendered inspection was not performed in run 001 under the host capacity directive. This run the load average was 0.54/0.94/1.07 (well under the ~8 threshold), so the full build + render pass ran over the verified overlay: render-inspect exit 0 with zero defects across desktop 1280x900, narrow 360x780, A4 794px print emulation and SVG glyph geometry, plus the reviewer's own visual inspection of three renders. Evidence: logs-agent-g3-gict300-u3-run002/render-review.txt and renders-agent-g3-gict300-u3-run002/.

PRESERVED FROM RUN001 (bank byte-identical): MCQ answer-position bias - 8 of 10 correct answers are option b, one is c (MCQ-05), one is d (MCQ-01), none is option a, confirmed by this reviewer's independent solve. Each item's key is correct and unambiguous, but the distribution is exploitable by a test-wise learner. Balance key positions across a/b/c/d at the next authoring touch.

PRESERVED FROM RUN001 (bank byte-identical): ERQ-01..04 restate the four per-topic Summative tasks nearly verbatim (biometric attendance, office rescue plan, print fault, staff-meeting explainer). The blueprint is satisfied and the rubrics are sound, but a learner who completed the topic tasks meets the same prompts again in the bank. Vary the context or scenario details at the next authoring touch.

Misquotation introduced by the F1 repair: the excerpt quotes "A file is simply a linear sequence of bytes that you can read and/or write". The book's actual sentence (OSTEP file-intro.pdf, section 39.1, fetched from the book's own site and verified this run) is "A file is simply a linear array of bytes, each of which you can read or write." The excerpt's wording appears nowhere in the chapter (mechanically verified over the extracted chapter text); "array" became "sequence" and "each of which you can read or write" became "that you can read and/or write". The meaning is identical and the underlying claim is sound, but the excerpt's own header states its passages are quoted, so a paraphrase inside quotation marks is a citation-integrity defect in the unit's bound evidence chain - the same class of defect run001 blocked on, now confined to one sentence. Repair: restore the book's verbatim sentence.

Taught-and-assessed sub-claims with neither bound-excerpt support nor disclosure. (a) Buffer and spooling (topic-03.mdx:54-59; concept CON:GICT-300-3-10; assessed by RRQ-10 and the unit summary): mechanically verified this run to have ZERO occurrences of "buffer" or "spool" in any of the three bound OSTEP chapters, and no other bound excerpt or declaration covers them. (b) Metadata (topic-02.mdx:45-47) and deletion semantics (topic-02.mdx:52-54): carried by the REAL chapter 39 (section 39.9 "Getting Information About Files" - size, ownership, access/modification times; section 39.14 unlink/reference-count mechanics), both verified this run against the book's site, but not included in the bound excerpt, and no declaration discloses them as uncorroborated. The ostep Supports cells in sources/unit-03.md are accurately scoped and do not overclaim, but under the G3 rubric a declaration that understates what it leaves unchecked remains a failure, and these are assessed concepts, not passing phrases. Repair (minimal): extend the chapter 39 excerpt with the real 39.9 metadata passage (and optionally the unlink/reference-count passage) verbatim; add buffer and spooling to the title-level disclosures in ## Unverifiable sources (they are classic Norton / Shelly & Vermaat material, both already-declared guide-required monographs) or record the gap per the style guide's scholarly-engagement rule.

After the coverage remap, Topic 3.2's file-management half (U3-03) is grounded in OSTEP chapter 39, but the topic's Further reading still cites only chapter 4 (the process chapter). The learner-facing reading pointer is now stale relative to the unit's own grounding. Add chapter 39 to the Topic 3.2 Further reading entry at the next authoring touch.

The bourgeois2019 excerpt's chapter-3 "Used for" annotation lists only U2-06/U2-07, while sources/unit-03.md now claims bourgeois2019 supports U3-01 (the three-part job) and U3-02 (named operating systems) from chapter 3. The chapter text does carry both claims (the three key functions and the Linux naming are verbatim in the bound excerpt - verified this run); only the excerpt's own annotation is stale. Update the annotation to include U3-01/U3-02 at the next touch.

The unit's primary excerpt ostep.md is NOT digest-bound in the input manifest: the ADR-0027 citedKeys derivation binds sources/texts/<key>.md only for keys matching a 4-digit-year pattern, and the key "ostep" has no year, so the excerpt that now grounds U3-01/U3-03/U3-04/U3-05 (and reinforces U3-06) sits outside every report's freshness binding - a later edit to it would not invalidate the reports that relied on it. Corpus-wide pattern, not unit-specific authoring: wipoIP.md (unit 5's excerpt) has the same year-less key. This review mitigates the gap by recording the excerpt's verified committed state (git blob e4822ccb99dc8fe7ce22df187221fb177a37922c, worktree clean) and by verifying its content directly against the book's site. The parent/owner should close the gap before a pass disposition rests on the excerpt: either rename the key to a year-carrying form in coverage/unit-03.md, sources/unit-03.md and the content-spec Mapped readings line, or have the owner amend the derivation in scripts/lib/review-evidence.mjs (an owner decision - amending a bound validator invalidates outstanding reports).

The Further reading source links render the bare URL as the link text (e.g. "https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~remzi/OSTEP/") on all four topic pages - render-inspect's bareUrlLinks advisory, confirmed in the desktop renders. A screen-reader user hears the raw URL; descriptive link text (the book or library page title) would be better. Advisory only; consistent with the corpus's current house pattern.
